mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, which in turn results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within three months signals an improving labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5% within three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% over three months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where RSAFS increases by more than 1% within three months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over three months signals increased economic activity and supply-side strength, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO increases by more than 2% within three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment (CPIAUCSL growth < 2% annually) signals a stable monetary policy, which reduces uncertainty and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of low-inflation (<2% annual growth) periods.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% each within three months signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases & UNRATE decreases > 0.5% each in 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where both PAYEMS and UNRATE meet the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over three months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where HOUST decreases by more than 10% within three months.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in real GDP (GDPC1) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 1% and 0.5% respectively within six months signals a robust economic expansion, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 1% & UNRATE decreases > 0.5% in 6 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where both GDPC1 and UNRATE meet the trigger conditions.
